summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, rheumatoid arthritis, chronic kidney disease, and hypertension was admitted for left-sided headache, facial tingling, tongue heaviness, and left arm weakness. Initial evaluation ruled out acute stroke with normal CT and MRI brain and MRA of the head and neck. Symptoms resolved during admission. She was found to have acute on chronic kidney failure, likely due to dehydration, with elevated creatinine and potassium. Treatment included IV fluids and kayexalate. Her meloxicam was held initially, leading to a rheumatoid arthritis flare, but was restarted at a lower dose with improvement. Blood pressure was managed with restart of valsartan and addition of amlodipine. Statin was increased for lipid control. She stabilized, kidney function improved, and she was discharged home with follow-up arranged for ongoing monitoring of kidney function and vascular risk factors.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
